issues.legal_issue: A contract to sell agricultural land is enforceable even if performance may leave the purchaser holding land beyond the applicable ceiling.
material_facts: The parties, who were both agriculturists, agreed to sell jirayat land.
The purchaser already held land, and the parties proceeded on the footing that acquiring the agreed land could cause the purchaser’s holding to exceed the ceiling.
The agreement itself did not transfer title, and the court found no indication that the agreement’s object was to defeat the law.
The purchaser could have disposed of existing land before acquiring title to the agreed land.
issues.conclusion: The contract was not void merely because its performance might result in the purchaser holding land beyond the ceiling, and the seller could not resist specific performance on that ground.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 23 of the Contract Act, an agreement is unlawful if its consideration or object is forbidden by law or would, if permitted, defeat the provisions of law. Sections 5, 34 and 35 of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948 prescribed a ceiling and provided for invalidity of an acquisition to the extent it resulted in excess holding; section 84C provided for the excess land to vest in the Government following the competent authority’s order. The Act did not generally prohibit a contract to transfer agricultural land between agriculturists. Under the Transfer of Property Act, an agreement to sell does not itself create an interest in the land. The court cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and agricultural_land_sale and parties_are_agriculturists and transfer_not_generally_prohibited and buyer_may_exceed_ceiling and no_purpose_to_defeat_law

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A party brought a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement to sell land.
predicates.agricultural_land_sale: The agreement concerned the sale of agricultural land.
predicates.parties_are_agriculturists: Both parties to the agreement were agriculturists.
predicates.transfer_not_generally_prohibited: The applicable legal framework did not generally prohibit the parties from transferring this land to one another.
predicates.buyer_may_exceed_ceiling: The purchaser’s existing holding and the land to be acquired could together exceed the applicable ceiling.
predicates.no_purpose_to_defeat_law: The court found no indication that the parties intended the agreement to defeat the law.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance suit concerns a permitted sale of agricultural land between agriculturists, and the purchaser may exceed the ceiling without an object to defeat the law, the contract remains enforceable despite the possible excess holding.

issues.legal_issue: A civil court may entertain and decree a suit for specific performance of an agreement to sell land even though a designated administrative authority decides whether a completed acquisition is invalid under the land-ceiling law.
material_facts: The purchaser sued in a civil court for specific performance of an agreement to sell land and for possession.
The purchaser had not acquired title under the agreement when the court was asked to decide whether to grant specific performance.
The statutory framework assigned the determination of whether a transfer or acquisition was invalid, and the disposal of the land, to the Mamlatdar after acquisition of title.
issues.conclusion: The civil court had jurisdiction to entertain and decree the suit for specific performance, although it had no jurisdiction to determine whether the acquisition was invalid under the Act.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 70(mb) and 85 of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948 reserved to the specified authorities questions assigned to them under the Act. Section 84C empowered the Mamlatdar to determine whether a transfer or acquisition was invalid and to deal with the land accordingly. That inquiry could take place only after acquisition of title; nothing in those provisions excluded civil-court jurisdiction over a suit for specific performance of the contract. The court cited no earlier cases.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A party brought a civil suit seeking specific performance of an agreement to sell land.
predicates.title_not_yet_acquired: The purchaser had not acquired title to the land when the court considered whether to enforce the agreement.
predicates.legal_framework_assigns_acquisition_vali: The applicable legal framework assigned the decision on the validity of a completed acquisition to an administrative authority.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance suit is brought before title is acquired and the legal framework assigns the validity of a completed acquisition to an administrative authority, the civil court may decree specific performance.
